items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: you remember Adam Clayton Powell. The first political advisor he had was my uncle

ctx.x: So, that's how I made it in New York City. And plus the fact that I usually try to help people. Then you know, you remember Adam Clayton Powell. The first political advisor he had was my uncle and this is how I happened to go into the political arena. I had a license on Broadway as a booking agent. Legitimate booking agent. Not, you know, sub-booking for somebody or, you know, I'm waiting for it to be approved.
I had an office at 1674 Broadway. That's where I gave Willie 'the Lion' and James P. Johnson an office just to come and play...

items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: So then we had a big reunion and on the boat, and then I met Adam Powell.

ctx.x: Now, he had not heard from us from 1913 to 1937...'38. I said, "I am your sister's son." And he was a dark man. He turned snow white for a moment. And he was flabbergasted when he found out who I was and that it was real. It took me a moment to say, "Well now your father's name was Albert and your mother's name was Mary Jane. And then I started naming his sisters...you know, flashbacks, to acquaint him with, you
know, who was what and what. So then we had a big reunion and on the boat, and then I met Adam Powell. And this was my introduction to the political arena.

He managed Adam's political affairs and he was also District Leader and he was in the Borough President's office, and he was a kingmaker, of course. He never sought any political office, but people running for office always tried to get his support in order to, you know, function and to be successful. And he helped to elect Roosevelt.../this was about the time/ well, the last time we re-elected Roosevelt and then he died. And Roosevelt died at the time that my uncle had helped me get this booking agency license.…
